budget_items.what_was_said: The parent-teacher organization donated funds to each school, left to each principal's discretion, and the committee voted to accept three such donations.
The superintendent described a one-time, non-recurring earmark from state legislators that cannot be added to the base budget; the captions gave inconsistent figures for the total and its two pieces.
The superintendent proposed spending part of the earmark on touch screens for every primary school classroom, the only school without them, replacing projectors.
The superintendent proposed restoring I-Ready diagnostic and instructional access for at least one more year; asked the cost, she said it was about 47.

The district considered using the earmark for smaller transportation vans instead, but determined the cost would exceed the available money and require driver stipends and special licenses, so it was not pursued.
Members noted the athletic fee was previously increased and is intended to partially cover uniform costs, though it does not cover the full cost.

The district previously cut a single dedicated Wilson reading position at Turkey Hill and instead used training funds to certify multiple inclusion teachers district-wide in the Wilson reading system.

Members discussed that compensation, especially for paraprofessionals, is weak compared to other districts, making positions hard to fill, though the superintendent cited staff loyalty to Lunenburg as a mitigating factor.

budget_items.topic: Teacher and instructional staff retention rate
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent set a goal of 90% or higher staff retention; last year's rate, which included layoffs, was described as concerningly low.
A member asked about anticipated multi-year budget impacts as union contracts, capped at three-year terms, come up for renewal; the business manager is building this into the long-term forecast.
The superintendent said she is conservatively forecasting entitlement grant funding to come in lower next year given uncertainty at the federal level.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill Elementary renovation cost estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: A member cited a prior renovation estimate for Turkey Hill, calling it likely too low, while pushing the committee to commit to a renovate-or-rebuild direction.
A warrant article is expected proposing the school committee give up budget responsibility for Kids Kingdom; a member said this would make the school budget more realistic.

The committee will talk with the facilities director about Turkey Hill as a next step.

minutes.headline: Committee reversed itself, voting to let soccer teams wear the new uniforms already purchased
minutes.summary: The School Committee accepted PTO donations, a state legislative earmark for primary-school touch screens and restoring I-Ready, and reversed a prior vote to release new soccer uniforms to players this season. The bulk of the meeting covered an assessment/accountability report showing concerning third-grade reading and special-education scores linked partly to prior budget cuts, followed by the superintendent's FY28 budget priorities, her first-year evaluation goals, and a discussion setting draft committee goals around Turkey Hill's future, capital planning, and a more reasoned budget-decision process.

what_happened.line: The committee reversed a prior vote and released the already-purchased soccer uniforms to players this season.
It voted to accept a one-time state legislative earmark, putting part of it toward primary-school touch screens and restoring the I-Ready assessment tool.
An accountability report described concerning third-grade reading and special-education subgroup scores, tied in part to earlier budget cuts.
The superintendent presented her FY28 budget priorities and first-year evaluation goals, both set for a formal vote next month.
The committee accepted three PTO donations to the schools.

why_it_matters: The uniform reversal and one-time earmark spending do not set district policy, but the FY28 budget priorities laid out here will shape the budget request residents are eventually asked to fund.
The reading and special-education score concerns, and the earlier cuts they were linked to, bear on how much the district asks for in literacy and special-education funding next year.
Weak paraprofessional pay and looming union contract renewals were raised as pressures the FY28 budget will need to absorb.
watch_next: Superintendent's first-year evaluation goals, a formal committee vote next meeting
FY28 budget town halls at each school, scheduled for mid-November

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.coverage: official minutes are a summary only
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every vote's outcome and on the core facts behind each (donations, grants, uniforms, tabling subcommittee reports), but the official minutes are a brief topic-by-topic summary that omits almost all the numeric/discussion detail our minutes captured from the recording (retention rates, compensation percentages, van funding, Turkey Hill cost estimate, several attendees). The one thing a reader should double-check is the earmark grant total (our captions say "$15,000" where the official minutes say "$105,000") and whether "Mr. Von" is actually Norman Yvon, principal of Turkey Hill Elementary rather than the Primary School as our minutes label him.
